current.text: Garland starts at point guard for the Clippers.
Kawhi Leonard, James Harden and Ivica Zubac have left the Clippers. Garland is the highest-usage player left on the roster.
He should be the main ball handler and compete with Brandon Ingram for the top usage spot. Garland and Ingram are expected to do nearly everything on offense.
Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal are out injured now.
Experts expect around 30% usage and at least the output he had with the Clippers last season, possibly more with Kawhi gone.
With the Clippers last season he played about 30 minutes a night with about 20 points and 7 assists on 29% usage, and ranked 37th per game after the deadline.
A toe injury limited him last season.
He is expected to be ready for opening night. The Clippers need 70 or more games from him.
If healthy he should play about 32 minutes. A small drop in three-point percentage is an acceptable trade for more minutes and usage.
Experts see a likely top 30 player, with a top 20 ceiling if he stays healthy.
Experts call him good value in the 40s or round 3. Taking him in the 30s is risky.
Experts say his market ADP is too late for his quality on both Yahoo and ESPN.
In an auction mock Josh set a max of 30 USD, which he called aggressive. A price of 25 USD was a little under his value.
He is the Clippers' best player and best fantasy target. A rookie guard will not take his role.
The Clippers could be one of the worst teams and might rest him late in the season, but experts call that risk small and say his value outweighs it.
The Clippers do not control their own draft pick, so tanking does not help them.
The Clippers play 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks and have 13 back-to-backs, one of the lowest totals in the league.

durable.text: He has persistent toe and knee problems and has also had a broken face.
His production drops for a long time after any injury, so he is hard to trust unless he is fully fit.
He is an electric offensive player and a below-average defender.
Assists are his standout category and a league outlier. He also helps in threes, points and FT%.
Turnovers are a clear weakness, high even for a guard.

note: Garland is an assist-led guard who also gives threes, points and FT%, but his turnovers are high. That makes him a natural fit for punt TO builds. Yahoo values him at 19 USD with an average cost of only 8 USD, ESPN values him at 9 USD, and he went for 11 USD in our league last season. Experts see a top 30 player at a round 3 price, so paying in the high teens is reasonable and 25 USD is about the ceiling. Early in the season, check that his toe holds up, that he plays at least 32 minutes, and how his usage changes while Ingram is out and after he returns.
